title: No Measurable Benefit from Verifier‑Assisted Generate→Validate→Repair under Shared‑Initial Generation: A Preregistered Emulation Study
abstract: We preregistered and autonomously executed a paired emulation study (study‑cnd‑2026‑001) to evaluate whether a verifier‑assisted generate→validate→repair pipeline increases oracle pass rates for LLM‑produced network configurations in vendor‑diverse emulated NetOps tasks. The frozen design used shared_initial_candidate generation semantics (one generator call per pair consumed by both conditions), declared model gpt‑5‑mini, a deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5), and a repair budget ≤1 call/task. Execution produced 200 complete pairs (400 episodes) and model_calls_used=200. Results: baseline = 200/200 oracle passes; guarded = 200/200 oracle passes; paired difference = 0.00 (paired bootstrap 95% CI [0.00,0.00], bootstrap_resamples=10000, seed=1729); McNemar two‑sided p = 1.00. The null result is design‑bound: because each preregistered shared candidate passed the deterministic oracle, the repair stage was never exercised. We release the full audited artifact bundle (preregistration, prompts, raw outputs, provider traces, validator traces, execution manifest and SHA‑256 digests) and provide artifact‑anchored recommendations for informative follow‑ups (independent generation semantics, calibrated difficulty, larger repair budgets, validator stress tests).

sections.introduction: Generative LLMs are being explored as intent→configuration agents for network operations (NetOps). Operational correctness is critical: configurations must preserve safety invariants (protected interfaces, minimum‑up counts, make‑before‑break for uplinks), vendor idioms, and transient safety during change. A common mitigation architecture is generate→validate→repair: models propose configurations, deterministic validators (oracles) check objective properties, and when the oracle fails a repair module attempts corrective synthesis. Prior work documents practical gains from validator‑guided constraints and verifier‑grounded repair in program synthesis and domain tasks, motivating rigorous, preregistered measurement of how much verifier assistance reduces misconfiguration in NetOps. We designed and froze study‑cnd‑2026‑001 to answer this question under an explicitly declared experimental semantics and to archive every artifact for reproducible audit.
sections.related_work: The evidence base for verifier‑assisted generation in NetOps and analogous domains is growing. Constraint‑guided oracles and stateful validators have been applied to network configuration generation and Kubernetes policy (e.g., verifier‑centric workflows), while verifier‑grounded repair has improved correctness for program and DSL generation (StruSpec). Benchmarks for intent→configuration translation (NetConfEval, intent‑based networks) and constraint‑augmentation architectures (MeshAgent) motivate our experimental architecture. Crucially, many prior reports mix generator variance and verifier interventions without preregistered generation semantics; our run freezes those semantics and archives primary artifacts to make the experimental boundary explicit (see cited_record_ids).
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and frozen plan: We preregistered study‑cnd‑2026‑001 (SHA‑256 a8969ac01f3b1bb7585872c58a92f72d0752160dd4e6e01cbafbfe0d15073ad2) and froze: primary_estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate; declared model = gpt‑5‑mini (adapter family hosted_netops_gvr_v1); validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5; maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1; paired Npairs = 200. The master prompt that initiated the autonomous post‑lock run is archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba).

Task bank and stratification: The preregistered task manifest contains 200 paired tasks stratified by protocol and vendor: four protocol buckets (BGP/OSPF/ACL/VLAN, 50 pairs each) and per‑protocol vendor allocation Cisco=17, Juniper=17, Arista=16 (execution/task_manifest.jsonl; artifact hashes recorded in execution manifest). Complexity was balanced (simple=100, complex=100). Each manifest entry includes: intent text, initial and expected final states, required_sequence constraints, and a reference_answer. Representative task artifacts (e.g., execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json, SHA‑256 eaf96aec...) show the explicit intent, required command sequence, and validator trace used for scoring.

Generation semantics, model use, and adapter: The frozen generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate required a single generator call per paired test; that single generated candidate was delivered unchanged to both baseline and guarded scorers. The declared generator was gpt‑5‑mini via the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter (execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 1acce925...). The execution manifest records model_calls_used=200 (one shared generation per 200 pairs) and provider call traces under execution/provider_calls/ with per‑file SHA‑256 digests.

Validator, repair policy, and scoring: The deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) parses candidate configurations, simulates their effect on a deterministic emulated network model, and returns a normalized_configuration, valid boolean, parsed_command_count, violation list, and a validator trace. Repair was permitted up to one call per task but, in this run, repair_applied = false for all pairs and repair calls invoked = 0 (execution and scoring artifacts record this). Scoring files (execution/scoring/*.json) contain the full validator trace used in analysis.

Statistical analysis (frozen): The preregistered analysis executor paired_binary_analysis_v1 performed paired bootstrap percentile inference (10,000 resamples, seed=1729) for a 95% CI on the paired success‑rate difference and an exact McNemar two‑sided test for discordant pairs. All analysis inputs and outputs are archived (analysis/*) with SHA‑256 digests for audit.
sections.results:
Execution and scoring summary (artifact‑backed): The autonomous run completed all planned episodes: planned_episode_count=400, completed_episode_count=400, failed_episode_count=0, model_calls_used=200 (execution/execution_manifest.json). Scoring summary (analysis/condition_summary.csv SHA‑256 1cb072b4...): baseline_success_count = 200/200 (100%); guarded_success_count = 200/200 (100%). The paired contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 7bc1bd2a...) is n11=200, n10=0, n01=0, n00=0.

Confirmatory inference (artifact: analysis/results.json): paired difference = 0.00; paired bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.00,0.00] (bootstrap_resamples=10000, seed=1729); McNemar two‑sided p = 1.00. Analysis log (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl SHA‑256 940b48e7...) documents the exact bootstrap parameters and confirms the paired analysis completed with complete_pair_count = 200.

Representative diagnostic example (artifact grounding): execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json (SHA‑256 eaf96aec...) shows: intent summary, required_sequence (four ordered commands), shared_initial_candidate (the generated lines), parsed_command_count=4, final_state dictionary, valid=true, and repair_applied=false. Equivalent guarded artifact for the same pair is execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json (SHA‑256 b8b05283...). The equality of shared_initial_candidate in both condition artifacts and validator valid=true is the proximate cause of the degenerate contingency.

Deterministic reconciliation: analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json (SHA‑256 799b23b9...) confirms internal accounting and mapping: complete_pair_count=200; baseline_from_contingency=200; guarded_from_contingency=200; hosted_model_call_event_count=200; cache_hit_count=0; cache_miss_count=200; all deterministic consistency checks passed. Every scoring record maps to a stored raw response and provider trace (execution/execution_manifest.json contains the full per‑file hash manifest).
sections.discussion:
Causal interpretation: The preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics produced one generated candidate per pair that both conditions consumed. In every pair that single shared candidate satisfied the deterministic validator, so the repair stage never ran (repair_calls_invoked = 0). The observed null difference therefore reflects a preregistered design boundary (ceiling effect), not a general statement about verifier‑assisted repair efficacy. The artifacts—generation traces, scoring JSONs, and the deterministic reconciliation file—document this causal chain unambiguously.

Statistical and operational implications: Perfect concordance (all pairs passing) yields zero empirical variance on the paired difference, producing a degenerate bootstrap CI and a McNemar test with no discordant pairs (p=1.00). These are the correct inferential consequences under the frozen estimand. Operationally, measuring repair effectiveness requires that initial candidates sometimes fail the validator or that independent generation provide differing initial candidates per condition so repairs can act.

Practical, artifact‑anchored follow‑ups (executable from archived materials): The current artifact bundle supports two immediate, reproducible experimental variants that will permit repair intervention and measure verifier benefit: (1) independent_per_condition generation semantics — change the preregistration to generate one candidate per condition per pair (expected model_calls ≈ 400), then rerun using the same task manifest seeds; this exposes generator variance and allows repair to act when baseline candidates fail; (2) calibrated difficulty upgrade — expand task_manifest.jsonl with higher‑difficulty tasks or boundary constraints (e.g., stricter minimum_up counts, transient invariants) so a fraction of shared candidates fail the validator. Both variants reuse the archived prompts, validator, and analysis executor and will be hash‑tracked in the same reproducible framework. Additional operational variants include increasing maximum_repair_calls_per_task (>1), enabling iterative repair loops, and executing across multiple generator models (multi‑model replication) to test generality. Each variant is directly implementable from the archived artifacts and manifests and should be recorded with new preregistrations to preserve auditability.

Threats to validity (artifact‑grounded): Internal validity — the dominant internal threat is the frozen generation semantics; prompt sensitivity is recorded in provider traces and can be audited (execution/provider_calls/*). Construct validity — the deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) enforces emulation‑based safety predicates; oracle blind spots remain possible and are flagged where present in validator traces (violation lists, validation_before metadata). External validity — the run used a single declared model (gpt‑5‑mini) and emulated deterministic device behavior; extrapolation to production devices or other models is limited. Conclusion validity — the paired design and analysis executor were executed as frozen; inference is exact for the frozen estimand but degenerate because repairs were not exercised.
sections.conclusion: Under the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics and the frozen task bank, verifier assistance produced no measurable improvement because the single shared generated candidate per pair passed the deterministic oracle in every case. The result emphasizes that study design choices (generation semantics, task difficulty, repair budget) critically determine whether a verifier or repair module can be exercised and measured. We publish the full immutable artifact bundle (preregistration, master prompt reference, raw outputs, provider traces, validator traces, execution manifest and per‑file SHA‑256 digests) so future runs can (a) adopt independent generation semantics and calibrated difficulty to permit repair invocation, and (b) repeat the test across models and iterative repair policies to measure operationally meaningful verifier benefit.

limitations: The confirmatory conclusions apply only to the exact preregistered design (shared_initial_candidate semantics, declared model gpt‑5‑mini, deterministic_netops_validator_v5, synthetic/emulated 200‑pair task bank).

Shared_initial_candidate semantics created a ceiling effect: because the single shared generated candidate per pair passed the deterministic oracle for every task, the repair stage was never invoked (repair calls invoked = 0), preventing measurable guarded benefit in this run.
Emulation with a deterministic validator and synthetic tasks does not capture production heterogeneity (real vendor images, runtime nondeterminism, device‑specific quirks).
Single‑model execution limits generality across model families and instruction‑tuning variants.
Repair budget was intentionally limited (≤1 call/task) by preregistration; richer iterative repair policies remain unexplored in this run.
Oracle blind spots (uncovered semantic failure modes) remain possible; oracle‑coverage diagnostics are archived in validator traces and should be reviewed in follow‑ups.
